title: uewf-atlantic
label: Admiral Ax

won.source: the Summit of E-Wrestling's own broadcast of 28 December 1991 (promotions/summit-of-e-wrestling/archive/summit-of-e-wrestling-day-2-1991-12-28.html), whose ring announcer sets the terms before the bell: "the winner to move on to the finals of this tournament and the loser to be named the UEWF's first Atlantic Champion."

how: The first reign on this belt, and the federation's own first Atlantic Champion. Awarded on 28 December 1991 for losing a World Championship semi-final that was announced in advance as crowning a champion either way: Mr. B won the match by disqualification when the referee found the roll of quarters Admiral Ax had punched him with, and the belt went to the loser. FOUND BY THE SUMMIT ACCESSION, 2026-09-02, which supersedes the earlier reading that this belt's first reign was the one the May 1992 relaunch call recognised — that reign is renumbered r002 and now stands second. How the belt passed from this holder to the next is not on the record and no date is invented for it.
note: HOW THIS REIGN ENDED IS NOW ON THE RECORD, and the row's own line that it is not is superseded: the WeWF's own newsdesk of 15 February 1992 prints this federation's standings with “Atlantic Champion: vacant”, and the same table has this holder holding the Intercontinental Championship instead. He left the belt rather than lost it. Biff “the Terror” Jones filled the vacancy four days later.

how: Won the vacant championship by pinning Mosh; lost it six days later to Pain.
note: THIS REIGN AND THE VACANCY BEFORE IT WERE BOTH MISSING FROM THIS LEDGER, which ran the belt straight from Admiral Ax to Pain. The newsdesk's own standings of 15 February 1992 read “Atlantic Champion: vacant”.

how: Recognised as champion at the federation's own relaunch of 14 May 1992, which reinstates "the wrestlers who were champions before the UeWF's hiatus." No served document carries a match or a date for the start of this reign; the federation's own first title tournaments were staged at the Summit of E-Wrestling in December 1991, and the Summit accession of 2026-09-02 shows they settled the Atlantic, the Pacific and the Ladies belts and left this one alone. This holder was named the federation's first ATLANTIC Champion on 28 December 1991; when he took this belt instead is not something any served document says. Four days after the relaunch call the same president wrote that all the champions were returning "with the exception of 2" — which two is not on record, so no reign here is ended on that sentence. THE HELD-BUT-UNSERVED RECORD CARRIES THIS REIGN RUNNING, THOUGH NOT ITS START (2026-09-02). The WeWF's own broadcasts of 15, 19 and 25 February 1992 have this holder as Intercontinental Champion at 10-0-0, beating Lord Plunder to retain, and beating Rage to retain, ending that week at 14-1-0. So the reign is continuous from at least mid-February to the relaunch call's recognition in May. Its beginning is still nowhere in the record, served or unserved.
note: The reign is now bounded at both ends of the winter: Mr. B holds this belt on 30 January 1992 and this holder holds it by 15 February, defending it over Lord Plunder on 19 February and over Rage on 25 February, and standing at 14-1 in the last rankings the newsdesk printed.

title: uewf-pacific
label: Lord Plunder

won.source: the Summit of E-Wrestling's own broadcast of 28 December 1991 (promotions/summit-of-e-wrestling/archive/summit-of-e-wrestling-day-2-1991-12-28.html), whose ring announcer sets the terms before the bell: "The Winner will advance to face in the Championship round and the loser will be be awarded the Pacific Championship Title."

how: Awarded on 28 December 1991 for losing the second of the federation's own two World Championship semi-finals, staged at the Summit of E-Wrestling and announced in advance as crowning a champion either way. Lucifer beat Lord Plunder with the HellRaiser, after throwing a packet of dust in his eyes, and after a man the announcers took for a blind spectator had climbed onto the apron and drawn the referee away — the broadcast never says who he was, only that his tights read "Totally Awesome Dude"; the Pacific Championship went to the loser. The federation's own relaunch call of 14 May 1992 still recognises this holder as its Pacific Champion, so the reign runs from the Summit to at least that date. DATED BY THE SUMMIT ACCESSION, 2026-09-02, which supersedes this row's earlier "no served document carries a match or a date for the start of this reign" — one now does. Four days after the relaunch call the same president wrote that all the champions were returning "with the exception of 2" — which two is not on record, so no reign here is ended on that sentence. THIS REIGN IS NOT CONTINUOUS, AND THE HELD RECORD SAYS SO (2026-09-02). The sentence above has this reign running from the Summit to at least 14 May 1992. It did not. The WeWF's own broadcasts of 15 and 19 February 1992 — held, unserved — have T'ien "The Master" Lung as this federation's Pacific Champion, at 12-1-1 and defending successfully against the Shropshire Slasher, with this holder first among the contenders; the broadcast of 25 February then has this holder win the belt back, "Lord Pluder beat Pacific Champion T'ien 'The Master' Lung by hitting him with an internation object," and prints "Pacific Champion: Lord Plunder (12-4-0)". So the reign dated here to 28 December 1991 ended before mid-February 1992, and the holder the relaunch call recognises in May is in a SECOND reign that begins in the last week of February. The row is not renumbered and no second reign is minted, because the documents that carry it belong to another wing and are not served; the correction is written here so nothing in this ledger reads as settled when it is not.
note: THIS REIGN DID NOT RUN UNBROKEN TO MAY 1992 AND THE ROW SAID IT DID. T'ien “the Master” Lung holds the belt in the WeWF newsdesk's own standings for this federation on 30 January, 15 February and 19 February 1992; this holder wins it back on 25 February, and that second reign is the one the relaunch call recognises. How this first reign ended is not carried by any held document — a gap, not a claim.

how: Recognised as champion at the federation's own relaunch of 14 May 1992, which reinstates "the wrestlers who were champions before the UeWF's hiatus." No served document carries a match or a date for the start of this reign; the federation's own first title tournaments were staged at the Summit of E-Wrestling in December 1991, and the Summit accession of 2026-09-02 NARROWS THIS REIGN WITHOUT DATING IT: these holders reached the final of that inaugural tag-team tournament, beating Carnage on 30 December 1991, and the final itself — against the Armed Forces — was advertised for a fifth night no held document carries. Whether this reign began in that final or later is still not something any served document says. Four days after the relaunch call the same president wrote that all the champions were returning "with the exception of 2" — which two is not on record, so no reign here is ended on that sentence. THE HELD-BUT-UNSERVED RECORD CARRIES THIS BELT IN FEBRUARY 1992 AND CONTRADICTS ITSELF ABOUT IT (2026-09-02). On 15 February the Dangerous Emotions' own manager calls them "the first UeWF tag-team champions"; on 19 February the newsdesk has them lose by disqualification to the Armed Forces and keep the belts; on 25 February it has the Armed Forces keep the belts by losing by disqualification to the Dangerous Emotions. One of the two is a transposition or a title change nobody reported. Recorded, not resolved, and nothing minted: all three documents are the WeWF's own and none is served.
note: THAT THIS IS THE FIRST REIGN ON THIS BELT IS NOW SETTLED BY THE TEAM'S OWN MANAGER, on camera at the Boston Garden on 15 February 1992: “Now that my Emotions are the first UeWF tag-team champions, I want you to know that they will be the ONLY tag-team champions.” They retain by disqualification on 19 February and win by disqualification on 25 February.

title: uewf-ladies-world
label: Laurie Liberty

won.source: the Summit of E-Wrestling's own broadcast of 28 December 1991 (promotions/summit-of-e-wrestling/archive/summit-of-e-wrestling-day-2-1991-12-28.html): "The Winner and NEW UeWF Ladies Champion...... Laurie......LIB.....ERTY!!!!!!"

how: Won an eight-woman battle royal staged at the Summit of E-Wrestling to crown the federation's own first Ladies Champion: two women started and the other six entered at one-minute intervals, with the first and second ranked having had first pick of numbers five to eight, and elimination over the top rope only. Laurie Liberty drew last, was thrown over the top rope onto the apron and came back in through her opponent's legs, and won it by playing possum in the Angel of Death's grip and scooping her out. FOUND BY THE SUMMIT ACCESSION, 2026-09-02; the belt's own row had said no holder survived. No end to this reign is on the record: the federation's own relaunch call of 14 May 1992 closes the women's division rather than naming a champion, so the reign is left open and the division's closure is carried on the title row instead. THIS REIGN ENDED IN FEBRUARY 1992, AND THE ROW'S OWN "left open" IS CORRECTED HERE RATHER THAN ERASED (2026-09-02). The WeWF's own This Week in Wrestling of 19 February 1992 — held in the Google Groups dumps, unserved — cuts to a clip of this federation's ladies title match and ends it on "JAckson covers......ONE!....TWO.....THREEEE!!!! We've got a new champion"; the following week's edition has "Sarah Jackson kept her Women's belt, when Rhonda Rhodes interfered saving Ms. Jackson from a pinfall at the hands of Laurie Liberty." Sarah Jackson took this belt from this holder in the third week of February 1992. No end date is written onto this row and no second reign is minted, because the documents belong to another wing and are not served; what is written is that the record is no longer silent, only unserved.
note: THE ROW SAID “the reign is left open” AND IT IS NOT. Sarah Jackson beat this holder for the belt on 19 February 1992, in a finish the WeWF's own newsdesk rolled as tape, and kept it against her six days later.
